GDPR Compliance Kit for small businesses.

The GDPR expects you to keep records and to prove compliance. This kit gives you the registers, deadlines and checklist to do it, without hiring a consultant.

GDPR

What's in the kit

  • Guide — what applies in your country, how to set everything up and what to check every week
  • Step-by-step compliance checklist with GDPR article references and an automatic progress score
  • Records of Processing (Art. 30) with legal bases and retention periods
  • Data Subject Request log with an automatic one-month deadline and days-left counter
  • Data Breach log with the automatic 72-hour reporting deadline
  • Processors & DPA tracker for every service provider and contract
  • Cookie & tracker audit that flags cookies set without consent
  • Example entries in every register, so you see exactly how to fill it in

The rules it covers

  • Records and accountability

    Art. 5(2) and Art. 30 GDPR: you must be able to show what personal data you process, why and on which legal basis.

  • Requests and breaches

    Data subject requests are answered within one month (Art. 12(3)); notifiable breaches go to the authority within 72 hours (Art. 33).

  • Processors and cookies

    Service providers need a data processing agreement (Art. 28). Non-essential cookies need prior consent under the ePrivacy rules and national law.

  • Small and medium-sized businesses

  • Website and online shop owners
  • Data protection coordinators without a legal team

Questions about this kit

Does a small business really need records of processing?
Almost always. The exemption for businesses under 250 employees in Art. 30(5) GDPR does not apply if processing is regular, which is the case for customer, staff or newsletter data. The kit's register is built for exactly that situation.
How fast do I have to answer a data subject request?
Within one month of receipt. In complex cases it can be extended by two further months, but you must tell the person within the first month. The request log calculates the deadline and the days left automatically.
When must I report a data breach?
Within 72 hours of becoming aware of it, unless the breach is unlikely to result in a risk to people. You must document every breach either way, and the breach log does that, with the deadline calculated for you.
